faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.label: Frequently asked questions about CivicLens
faq.languagesAnswer: You can write in English, Urdu, Roman Urdu, or mix them. CivicLens is a prototype and its language support is simulated.
faq.category: Do I need to choose a complaint category?
faq.categoryAnswer: No. You can describe the issue in your own words. AI may recommend a category, and a human can review or correct that recommendation.
faq.aiAnswer: The prototype demonstrates how AI could identify language, organise details, estimate urgency, and recommend routing. It does not make final decisions.
faq.decisions: Who decides what happens to my complaint?
faq.decisionsAnswer: People review and make service decisions. AI recommendations include estimated confidence and can be corrected by authorised staff.
faq.incorrectFix: What if the reported fix is not right?
faq.incorrectFixAnswer: A citizen can reject a proposed resolution with a reason. The complaint reopens for further action; only citizen acceptance confirms resolution.
faq.dataSafety: How is my data kept safe?
faq.dataSafetyAnswer: This academic prototype uses mock data and is not a live government service. Do not enter sensitive personal information.

about.title: About CivicLens
about.lead: CivicLens is an academic Final Year Project prototype about multilingual civic complaints in Pakistan.
about.storyTitle: Make civic reports easier to understand, while keeping people in control.
about.missionBody: Explore how multilingual AI could help organise civic complaints and support accountable review without replacing human decisions.
about.problemBody: Residents may describe civic issues in English, Urdu, Roman Urdu, or mixed writing. This prototype explores how those reports could be understood and structured for human review.
about.limitsBody: CivicLens is not a live service or an official government portal. AI outputs are simulated recommendations; people remain responsible for decisions.
about.limitsLink: How decisions are made and what the limits are

preview.title: A clearer lens on civic workflows.
preview.lead: A shared visual foundation for multilingual civic intelligence—where AI recommends, people decide, and every decision stays accountable.
preview.positioningBody: CivicLens adds an intelligence and accountability layer to existing complaint workflows. It does not replace the services people already use.
preview.intelligence: Understand → Extract → Classify → Prioritise → Route → Detect related issues → Monitor SLA → Escalate → Verify resolution → Audit AI decisions
preview.principlesTitle: Trust is part of the interface.
preview.aiRecommendsBody: Recommendations show an estimated confidence, plain-language reason, and model version. Low confidence is sent for human review.
preview.originalSacredBody: The citizen’s exact text is preserved. Normalised text is a separate, clearly identified derived value.
preview.citizenVerificationBody: Staff submit a proposed resolution. Only the citizen can accept it; rejection reopens the case and records a reason.
preview.auditableBody: The append-only audit history records original AI values, human changes, reasons, actor, and time.

marketingShowcase.faqLead: A brief overview of the prototype’s role and boundaries.
marketingShowcase.faqQuestionOne: Does CivicLens replace existing complaint portals?
marketingShowcase.faqAnswerOne: No. It is an academic prototype exploring an intelligence and accountability layer for existing workflows.
marketingShowcase.faqQuestionTwo: Does AI make the final decision?
marketingShowcase.faqAnswerTwo: No. AI provides recommendations and estimates; authorised people review and decide.
marketingShowcase.faqQuestionThree: Are the statistics shown measured results?
marketingShowcase.faqAnswerThree: No. Any sample figures are marked as demo data and do not represent evaluation results.
